fluency_questions.prompt: Find the five-number summary ($\text{Min}, Q_1, Q_2, Q_3, \text{Max}$) and the Interquartile Range ($\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$) for each ordered dataset:
Sort each dataset first, then find the median ($Q_2$), range, and $\text{IQR}$:

A grouped frequency table of $40$ runner times (minutes) has intervals $20\text{--}<25$ ($f=5$), $25\text{--}<30$ ($f=11$), $30\text{--}<35$ ($f=15$), $35\text{--}<40$ ($f=6$), $40\text{--}<45$ ($f=3$). Find:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The modal class interval

parts.label: b
parts.question: The percentage of runners finishing in under $30$ minutes

parts.label: c
parts.question: The class interval containing the median ($20\text{th}$ and $21\text{st}$ runners)

parts.label: d
parts.question: The estimated mean time using class midpoints ($22.5, 27.5, 32.5, 37.5, 42.5$)

fluency_questions.prompt: Using the outlier fence rule ($\text{Lower} = Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$, $\text{Upper} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$), find both fences and test the given value:

parts.label: b
parts.question: $Q_1 = 50, Q_3 = 70$; test $x = 25$
parts.answer: Fences $20$ and $100$; $25$ is NOT an outlier

parts.label: d
parts.question: $Q_1 = 100, Q_3 = 140$; test $x = 195$
parts.answer: Fences $40$ and $200$; $195$ is NOT an outlier

application_questions.question: Two AFL teams record their points scored across $7$ matches: Team A: $74, 78, 82, 85, 88, 91, 95$; Team B: $52, 68, 75, 86, 98, 110, 122$. Find the median and $\text{IQR}$ for each team and state which team is more consistent.
application_questions.answer: Team A: $\text{Median}=85, \text{IQR}=13$; Team B: $\text{Median}=86, \text{IQR}=42$. Team A is much more consistent.

application_questions.question: The daily maximum temperatures ($^\circ\text{C}$) in Melbourne over $7$ days were $18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 38$. Calculate the mean and median, and explain which better represents a typical day.
application_questions.answer: $\text{Mean} = 23^\circ\text{C}$, $\text{Median} = 21^\circ\text{C}$; the median ($21^\circ\text{C}$) is better because the $38^\circ\text{C}$ heatwave outlier pulls the mean up.

application_questions.question: A back-to-back stem plot (key: $3 \mid 4 = 34$) has left-side leaves $8\; 5\; 1$ on stem $2$ for Group X. List the three data values represented for Group X.
A television network runs a paid SMS poll during a late-night sports show and claims '$85\%$ of Australians want longer seasons'. Identify two sources of sampling bias in this claim.
application_questions.answer: Voluntary response / self-selection bias (only viewers motivated to pay and text respond) and coverage bias (late-night sports viewers do not represent all Australians).

reasoning_questions.question: Why is the $\text{IQR}$ preferred over the range when comparing the spread of skewed datasets such as house prices or personal incomes?
reasoning_questions.answer: The range ($\text{Max} - \text{Min}$) is heavily distorted by a single extreme outlier, whereas the $\text{IQR}$ measures only the middle $50\%$ of scores and is resistant to extreme outliers.

reasoning_questions.question: A distribution of exam marks has $\text{Mean} = 64$ and $\text{Median} = 73$. Is the distribution positively skewed or negatively skewed? Explain why.
reasoning_questions.answer: Negatively skewed; a tail of very low scores pulls the mean downwards below the median ($\text{Mean} < \text{Median}$).

application_questions.question: A café in Canberra finds that hot chocolate sales $C$ relate to morning temperature $T$ ($^\circ\text{C}$, observed from $2^\circ\text{C}$ to $22^\circ\text{C}$) by $C = -4T + 110$. Predict sales at $T = 10^\circ\text{C}$ and $T = 32^\circ\text{C}$, and state which is reliable.
application_questions.answer: At $10^\circ\text{C}$: $70$ cups (reliable interpolation); at $32^\circ\text{C}$: $-18$ cups (impossible extrapolation)

application_questions.question: In a two-way survey, $80$ Year 8 students ($52$ play sport, $28$ do not) and $120$ Year 10 students ($60$ play sport, $60$ do not) are asked about sport participation. Compare the percentage playing sport in each year level.
application_questions.answer: Year 8: $65\%$; Year 10: $50\%$. There is an association: Year 8 students have a higher participation rate.

application_questions.question: A school has $180$ Year 7, $160$ Year 8, and $160$ Year 9 students ($500$ total). How many students from each year level should be chosen in a stratified sample of $50$ students?
Four data points $(2, 6), (4, 10), (6, 14), (8, k)$ have mean point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y}) = (5, 12)$. Find $k$.

reasoning_questions.question: A study shows a strong positive correlation between the number of coffee shops in a suburb and the number of libraries. Does opening more coffee shops cause more libraries to be built? Identify a lurking variable.
reasoning_questions.answer: No; the lurking variable is suburb population size (larger suburbs have more of both coffee shops and libraries).

reasoning_questions.question: Why should you compare row percentages rather than raw frequencies in a two-way table when the row totals are unequal?
reasoning_questions.answer: Raw counts are skewed by group size; converting each row to a percentage of its own total puts different-sized groups on a fair $0\%$ to $100\%$ scale.
